findings.title: Build and Enlist payment resource types are only unasked key extras
source_references: Rulebook PDF p18, BUILD: The resource used to build structures is wood.
Rulebook PDF p20, ENLIST: The resource used to enlist recruits is food.
findings.reason: The resource identity determines which stock can legally pay for the action. Q10 explicitly requests Upgrade and Deploy costs, but Q11 only requests Build locations, permanence and enemy-occupied Mill/Mine behavior. Q12 only requests recruit placement, bonuses and resolution. An answer can satisfy every requested part of Q11 and Q12 without stating wood or food. Their keys do contain those facts, which cannot establish elicitation. Q03 establishes the general exposed-red-box payment procedure; it does not request the action-to-resource mapping.
findings.severity: narrow but meaningful core-procedure coverage gap

proposed_additions.question: Which resource is used to pay for the Build action, and which is used to pay for the Enlist action?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Build uses wood. Enlist uses food; the amount required is the exposed cost on the corresponding Player Mat action.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p10, GAMEPLAY, exposed red-box costs
proposed_additions.novelty: Tests two previously unelicited core payment-resource identities in one parallel question, using the same pairing approach already used for Upgrade/Deploy in Q10. This adds no changed numerical quantity, artificial scenario, mechanical interaction, setup padding or cosmetic rewrite. Resource identity affects whether the player can legally take these bottom-row actions.
proposed_additions.existing_entries: Leave Q01-Q62 and all existing keys unchanged.

limitations: This review addresses the supplied 2016 booklet and base multiplayer scope only; no external FAQ or later-edition correction was used.

The PDF text was checked in full and required image-only numeric evidence was visually inspected on parent pages 19 and 29; other PDF illustrations were not separately treated as additional independent rules.
No claim is made that every explanatory sentence or routine physical-handling instruction needs an individual question. The proposed gap concerns the legal resource identity of two core actions.
Only this report file was written; the bank, keys and parent ledgers remain unchanged.
